newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian refugees arrive in Italy after lull.
newsitem.headline: Albanian refugees arrive in Italy after lull.

text.p: An Albanian military boat carrying 38 people docked in this south-eastern port on Saturday carrying the first refugees to arrive in Italy for more than three days.
Nearly 11,000 Albanians have sailed to Italy since March 13 in a flotilla of rusty old boats, but strong winds and heavy seas halted the exodus on Wednesday.
The lull was broken on Saturday afternoon when an Albanian patrol boat, carrying women and children as well as some navy personnel, reached Italian waters and was escorted into port by coastguards.
Port officials said another boatload of Albanians was expected to dock after nightfall with around 50 people aboard.

Italy said on Thursday it was holding negotiations with Tirana over the reactivation of navy patrols in Albanian waters to deter the exodus of people seeking to flee the armed unrest in the small Balkan state.
Rome also said on Friday it was preparing to send emergency health supplies to Tirana at the weekend at the request of Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.
ANSA newsagency said the equipment would probably be airlifted to Tirana on Sunday from Pisa. It will be the first large-scale aid sent to Albania since order collapsed at the start of this month.
The foreign ministry said the supplies, in the form of health kits, would be enough for 300,000 people for a month.

ANSA also reported that Italian armed forces were preparing to make military units available to the European Union as part of a multinational force and that military planners had identified three Albanian beaches where troops could be landed.
Eyewitnesses in Brindisi said a number of Italian naval vessels had recently docked at the port.
The defence ministry in Rome declined to comment on the report or on how the health supplies would be taken to Tirana.
